members.note: A copy: a UFUNCTION return is a value, and handing out the live array would let a caller resize the thing every row is indexed into.
Goes through SetItemObjects, which settles the selection and the subclass's index-keyed state against the source that is going away. AddTextItem is the same call for a text-only source.

The parallel text goes in at the SAME index, blank: GetItemLabel falls back to the object's name for an index the texts do not reach, which is right at the END of a shorter array and wrong in the middle of one.
One rebuild for the batch, through FScopedRebuildSuppression -- a COUNTER rather than a flag, because the batch calls are written in terms of each other.
The one the other three are written in terms of.
Takes the matching text with it: the two arrays are parallel, and shortening only one re-labels every row after the hole.
Indices collected, sorted, then removed from the BACK: every removal shifts what is after it, so ascending order would make each index after the first one wrong.
Objects decide the count when there are any; texts otherwise.
Empties both sources and clears the selection.
EUIListSelectionMode, the four answers UUIListView already spells.
A four-answer enum rather than UMG's float: the same question the scroll box and the scroll behaviour already answer with EDreamUIScrollDestination, so a project learns it once.
See bEnableProximateEntryNavigation.

This control rebuilds synchronously -- every setter that moves the source rebuilds before it returns -- so there is never a pending refresh to be told about. That is deliberate: it is what makes the list correct in a headless test and on the designer's first frame.
Computed from the row pitch, so it answers for an item whose row is not realized -- the only version that means anything while recycling.
Selects AND reveals, because a selection that is off screen is a selection nobody can see they made.
FDreamListStyle, resolved against the project style sheet. Get/SetStyle.
The list's style carries the bar's whole style, so one edit dresses the list and its bar together.

Two overlays inside the VIEWPORT, not the scrolled column: a fade that scrolled with the content would be a stripe travelling through the list. Each is awake only while the list is scrolled away from that end, so it says 'there is more this way' rather than being permanent decoration.

FDreamUIFaceBrush on the CONTROL, not in FDreamListStyle: the style struct is the shared look and is resolved against the project sheet, where a fade is a per-screen decision about one list's edges. A sheet switching it on for every list at once is not an edit anyone would make on purpose.

EDreamPanelOrientation, this library's two-value spelling. The control is rewritten in MAIN/CROSS axis terms rather than branching per call site: row pitch, content extent, window size, furniture, placement, offset, overscroll and the reveal all read one pair of helpers. Vertical is the default, so nothing existing moves. UDreamTreeView refuses it -- a tree's indent is measured across its rows, and UMG has no horizontal tree either.
The same enum the scroll box uses.
SingleToggle IS 'a second click on the chosen row clears it'. A separate flag would be a second answer to the same question.
Already on the base of every widget.
EndInertialScrolling at the FRONT of the selection road, so the row the player picked does not slide out from under the cursor while the click is still being handled.

Acts only when focus landed on the LIST itself: focus that already reached a row is focus doing exactly what this wants, and redirecting it would drag the player off the row they just navigated to. FocusSelectedRow is the same move as a callable, and answers false honestly when the selected item has no realized row.

ARRIVING at a list is already geometric nearest-neighbour -- FDreamUINavigationScroll and UDreamWidgetNavigation pick the nearest row by rect, for every control -- which is what the flag turns on in UMG, so there is no second mode to switch to. Once on a row, a press steps by item the way SListView::OnNavigation does (UDreamListRowButton asks the list first), and only a press with nowhere to go inside the list goes back to the scan. Arrival does not select; a step does, while bSelectItemOnNavigation is on.
See SetScrollIntoViewAlignment.
A list has one column, so across-the-line spacing only means anything on the tile view, which is where it lives.
The gap under a row, which is what one step down the column costs beyond its height.
In the bar's style, which FDreamListStyle::Bar carries -- the same field the scroll box reads.
Read off the resolved tile style; see the property row.
Read off the resolved list style; see the property row.
An index into the SOURCE, which survives a collapse where an object identity comparison per row would not. GetIndexForItem turns an object into one.
By index; the only call that can express a multi selection.
Comes back empty for a text-only source, which has no objects to answer with; GetSelectedIndices is the question to ask there.
True when the item currently has a row widget standing for it.
By index; GetIndexForItem turns an object into one.
By index, and computed from the row pitch so it answers for an unrealized row.
The eased reveal is a tween on the scroll behaviour; stopping it is stopping what is moving the content.
Takes raw pointers, because TArray<TObjectPtr<>> cannot be a UFUNCTION parameter.
Plus GetSelectedIndex for the anchor. A single-item getter would be the first element of a set the caller can already see.
Once in a row widget's life, after the subclass's own one-time hook, so a consumer sees a row that is already wired.
Fires after the selection has moved, so a handler asking GetSelectedIndex sees the answer the user just gave.

Uses the event system's DoubleClickTime, so a list and the text field beside it agree about the interval. Said at the second press, as UMG's is (Slate routes that press to OnMouseButtonDoubleClick, not to OnMouseButtonDown); the click that press ends in still follows, and OnItemClicked still fires for it.

Fired while the operation is still editable, so a consumer can put its own payload or tag on it. Carries the ITEM INDEX as well as the object, because a text-only source has no object to identify a row by.

Any drag, not only this list's own. Forwarded by the row's own drop target, which has known its pool slot since it was made -- the base's enter/leave carry only the operation, and searching for the row would have had to guess on leave, where the hovered flag is already down.
See BP_OnItemDragEnter.

Carries EDreamItemDropZone -- AboveItem, OntoItem, BelowItem -- resolved from where the pointer sat along the row's MAIN axis, so a horizontal list reads the seams as its left and right edges. The list does NOT re-order itself: what a drop means is the consumer's to decide, and a list that moved its own source would be guessing at an edit only the data's owner can make.
Fired when the drag ended with nothing accepting, decided from the OPERATION's bDropWasHandled -- the operation outlives the row, which a recycled row or a closed screen can destroy mid-flight.
Both edges, from the same two places that set the flag.

Driven by the row selectable's state, which is the one thing that already distinguishes a resting pointer from focus. Reports the ITEM, so a row re-bound under a resting pointer announces the new one.

Carries the anchor index; GetSelectedIndices is the whole answer in Multi. Fired for a click, a navigation step, the API, and a source edit that takes selected items away (once per edit, a batch being one) -- not for a selection that only moved to a new index with its item, which in UMG is no change either.

The EDGE: RefreshVisibleWindow keeps the previous realized set and announces only the arrivals, after every bind rather than inside the loop, so a handler asking what else is on screen gets the whole answer.
Carries the offset AND the visible fraction, because a consumer drawing its own position indicator needs both and can work out neither.
Latched on the first move that lands with nothing left to carry it: one call per gesture rather than one per frame of a flick.

Forwarded from UUIScrollView's new native drag-gesture broadcast, which carries the phase and whether it was a finger. From the behaviour rather than a second set of pointer subscriptions: the behaviour is what decides a gesture reaches these rows at all, and a list listening separately would announce touches for drags the behaviour refused.
See BP_OnListViewTouchStart.
See BP_OnListViewTouchStart.

Single-cast with a bool return, like the tree's children provider: this is a QUESTION, and two answers is an ambiguity nothing can resolve. Asked on BOTH the click road and the navigation road, or the two disagree about which rows exist. Deselecting is never vetoed -- a row that became unselectable while chosen has to be able to stop being chosen.

The gap between entries is appearance, so it lives in the list's style rather than on the control: FDreamListStyle::RowSpacing, along the list's main axis (between rows of a vertical list, between columns of a horizontal one).
